nis2-020-01.question: Has the management body formally approved the cybersecurity risk-management measures?
nis2-020-01.description: NIS2 Article 20 requires the management body to approve and oversee cybersecurity risk-management measures.
nis2-020-01.guidance: Present cybersecurity strategy to the board. Document approval in board minutes. Include risk appetite, budget, and KPIs.

nis2-020-02.question: Does the management body review cybersecurity status reports at least quarterly?
nis2-020-02.description: Regular board-level reporting ensures ongoing visibility of cybersecurity posture and emerging risks.
nis2-020-02.guidance: Produce quarterly dashboards: key metrics, recent incidents, compliance status, training completion, audit findings.

nis2-020-03.question: Have management body members completed cybersecurity training for their oversight role?
nis2-020-03.description: NIS2 mandates that management body members undertake training to gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks.
nis2-020-03.guidance: Schedule annual executive cybersecurity briefings. Cover threat landscape, regulatory obligations, and board responsibilities.

nis2-020-04.question: Is there a designated CISO or equivalent with direct reporting to senior leadership?
nis2-020-04.description: Clear accountability requires a dedicated security leader with authority and visibility at the executive level.
nis2-020-04.guidance: Appoint a CISO or Head of Security reporting to CEO or board. Define responsibilities, authority, and budget in writing.

nis2-21a-01.question: Is there a formal information security policy reviewed at least annually?
nis2-21a-01.description: A documented IS policy is the foundation. It must be reviewed and updated to reflect changes in threats and business.
nis2-21a-01.guidance: Create or update IS policy covering scope, objectives, roles, acceptable use, classification, and review schedule.

nis2-21a-02.question: Is an annual risk assessment conducted using a recognised methodology (ISO 27005, NIST RMF)?
nis2-21a-02.description: Systematic risk assessment identifies and prioritises threats. A recognised framework ensures completeness.
nis2-21a-02.guidance: Adopt ISO 27005 or NIST RMF. Document assets, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, and treatment plans.

nis2-21a-03.question: Are cybersecurity risks in the enterprise risk register with owners and treatment plans?
nis2-21a-03.description: Cyber risks must be integrated into enterprise risk management, not siloed in IT.
nis2-21a-03.guidance: Add cyber risks to the enterprise risk register. Score by likelihood and impact. Assign owners. Review quarterly.

nis2-21a-04.question: Are security roles and responsibilities clearly defined and communicated (RACI matrix)?
nis2-21a-04.description: Clear ownership prevents gaps. A RACI matrix maps who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed.
nis2-21a-04.guidance: Create a security RACI matrix. Communicate roles during onboarding and annual policy reviews.

nis2-21b-01.question: Is there a documented incident response plan covering detection through lessons learned?
nis2-21b-01.description: A complete IRP covers preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.
nis2-21b-01.guidance: Document IRP with phases, roles, communication templates, and escalation paths. Test annually.

nis2-21b-02.question: Are incident severity levels defined with escalation paths and response SLAs?
nis2-21b-02.description: Classification ensures proportionate response. SLAs set expectations for triage and resolution.
nis2-21b-02.guidance: Define severity levels (P1-P4). Map escalation paths. Set SLAs: P1 within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours.

nis2-21b-03.question: Are you registered with your national CSIRT and have you tested the 24-hour notification process?
nis2-21b-03.description: NIS2 requires early warning to the CSIRT within 24 hours of a significant incident.
nis2-21b-03.guidance: Register with national CSIRT. Document notification process. Run a tabletop exercise testing 24h notification.

nis2-21b-04.question: Is there an incident register documenting all events, investigations, and post-incident reviews?
nis2-21b-04.description: A register demonstrates accountability, enables trend analysis, and supports regulatory reporting.
nis2-21b-04.guidance: Use a ticketing system to log all incidents. Record: date, reporter, severity, investigation, resolution, lessons learned.

nis2-21b-05.question: Has the incident response plan been tested through tabletop exercises or simulations in the last 12 months?
nis2-21b-05.description: An untested IRP may fail under pressure. Regular testing validates procedures, roles, and communication flows.
nis2-21b-05.guidance: Conduct at least annual tabletop exercises simulating realistic scenarios. Include cross-functional teams. Document findings and update the IRP.

nis2-21c-01.question: Is there a documented BCP identifying critical functions, dependencies, and recovery priorities?
nis2-21c-01.description: A BCP ensures the organisation can maintain essential operations during and after a disruption.
nis2-21c-01.guidance: Conduct BIA to identify critical functions. Document dependencies, recovery priorities, and communication plans.

nis2-21c-02.question: Are there DR plans with defined RTO/RPO for all critical systems?
nis2-21c-02.description: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective define acceptable downtime and data loss.
nis2-21c-02.guidance: Define RTO/RPO per critical system. Document DR procedures including failover steps and responsible teams.

nis2-21c-03.question: Have BCP/DR plans been tested in the last 12 months (tabletop, simulation, or failover)?
nis2-21c-03.description: Untested plans may fail when needed. Regular testing validates procedures and builds muscle memory.
nis2-21c-03.guidance: Schedule annual BCP/DR tests. Start with tabletop exercises, progress to full failover tests for critical systems.

nis2-21c-04.question: Are backup restorations tested regularly and backup integrity verified?
nis2-21c-04.description: Backups are only useful if they can be restored. Regular testing verifies data integrity and recovery procedures.
nis2-21c-04.guidance: Test backup restoration monthly for critical systems. Verify data integrity. Document results and remediate failures.

nis2-21c-05.question: Is there a crisis communication plan covering internal notification, regulatory reporting, and media handling?
nis2-21c-05.description: During a crisis, clear communication is critical. Delays or misinformation worsen impact and may violate NIS2 notification requirements.
nis2-21c-05.guidance: Document communication templates, spokesperson designation, notification chains, and media handling procedures. Test during BCP exercises.

nis2-21d-01.question: Is there a formal process for assessing supplier cybersecurity posture?
nis2-21d-01.description: Supply chain attacks are a primary vector. Assessing suppliers before engagement reduces third-party risk.
nis2-21d-01.guidance: Require vendors to complete security questionnaires. Review SOC 2/ISO 27001 reports. Assess annually.

nis2-21d-02.question: Do contracts include NIS2-aligned security obligations (breach notification, audit rights)?
nis2-21d-02.description: Contractual obligations ensure suppliers maintain security standards and notify you of incidents.
nis2-21d-02.guidance: Add contract clauses: breach notification within 24h, right to audit, insurance, data residency, subprocessor approval.

nis2-21d-03.question: Is there a register of third-party integrations, access levels, and data processed?
nis2-21d-03.description: You cannot protect what you do not know. A complete register enables risk assessment and access control.
nis2-21d-03.guidance: Inventory all SaaS tools, APIs, vendor connections. Document: data accessed, owner, contract details, review date.

nis2-21d-04.question: Does third-party access require approval, MFA, time limits, and monitoring?
nis2-21d-04.description: Uncontrolled vendor access is a common breach vector. Strict controls limit exposure.
nis2-21d-04.guidance: Require formal approval for vendor access. Enforce MFA, set time-limited sessions, enable audit logging.

nis2-21e-01.question: Is there a formal vulnerability management policy with remediation timelines?
nis2-21e-01.description: A policy defines how vulnerabilities are identified, assessed, prioritised, and remediated within set timelines.
nis2-21e-01.guidance: Define remediation SLAs: Critical 24h, High 7d, Medium 30d, Low 90d. Track compliance. Use CVSS for scoring.

nis2-21e-02.question: Are security requirements verified during system acquisition, development, and maintenance?
nis2-21e-02.description: Security must be embedded in the SDLC, not bolted on. Requirements should be verified at each stage.
nis2-21e-02.guidance: Integrate security gates in SDLC: threat modelling, secure code review, SAST/DAST, penetration testing before release.

nis2-21e-03.question: Is there a responsible vulnerability disclosure process and dependency monitoring?
nis2-21e-03.description: A disclosure process handles reported vulnerabilities. Dependency monitoring catches known CVEs in libraries.
nis2-21e-03.guidance: Publish a security.txt / vulnerability disclosure policy. Monitor dependencies with Dependabot/Snyk. Review weekly.

nis2-21e-04.question: Are critical/high vulnerabilities remediated within defined SLAs?
nis2-21e-04.description: Identifying vulnerabilities is only useful if they are fixed. SLA compliance demonstrates operational maturity.
nis2-21e-04.guidance: Track SLA compliance metrics. Escalate overdue critical/high vulnerabilities to management. Report monthly.

nis2-21e-05.question: Are automated security scanning tools (SAST, DAST, dependency scanning) integrated into the CI/CD pipeline?
nis2-21e-05.description: Manual security reviews do not scale. Automated scanning catches common vulnerabilities early and consistently.
nis2-21e-05.guidance: Integrate SAST (e.g. SonarQube, Semgrep) and dependency scanning (Dependabot, Snyk) into CI/CD. Fail builds on critical findings.

nis2-21f-01.question: Are controls tested via audits, penetration tests, or red team exercises?
nis2-21f-01.description: Testing validates that controls work as intended. Without testing, compliance is theoretical.
nis2-21f-01.guidance: Conduct annual penetration tests. Perform internal audits quarterly. Consider red team exercises for critical systems.

nis2-21f-02.question: Are cybersecurity KPIs tracked (MTTD, MTTR, patch compliance, etc.)?
nis2-21f-02.description: KPIs provide objective measurement of security posture and identify areas needing improvement.
nis2-21f-02.guidance: Track: MTTD, MTTR, patch compliance rate, phishing click rate, training completion, open vulnerabilities count.

nis2-21f-03.question: Are audit findings tracked to remediation with owners and deadlines?
nis2-21f-03.description: Audit findings without follow-up provide no value. Tracking ensures accountability and closure.
nis2-21f-03.guidance: Log all audit findings in a tracker. Assign owners and deadlines. Review progress monthly. Escalate overdue items.

nis2-21f-04.question: Does a continuous improvement process feed audit/incident/threat intel into policy updates?
nis2-21f-04.description: Lessons learned should drive policy and control improvements. This closes the feedback loop.
nis2-21f-04.guidance: After audits and major incidents, update relevant policies and controls. Document changes and rationale.

nis2-21g-01.question: Is mandatory security training provided on hire and renewed annually?
nis2-21g-01.description: All staff must receive baseline security training. Annual renewal keeps knowledge current.
nis2-21g-01.guidance: Implement onboarding training covering: password policies, MFA, phishing, data handling, incident reporting. Renew yearly.

nis2-21g-02.question: Are phishing simulations conducted at least quarterly with results tracked?
nis2-21g-02.description: Simulated campaigns measure real-world readiness and identify individuals needing additional training.
nis2-21g-02.guidance: Run quarterly phishing simulations. Provide immediate feedback to clickers. Track metrics and trends over time.

nis2-21g-03.question: Is role-specific security training provided for technical staff?
nis2-21g-03.description: Engineers and admins need specialised training beyond general awareness (secure coding, cloud security).
nis2-21g-03.guidance: Provide training: Developers (OWASP, secure coding), Admins (least privilege, logging), Cloud engineers (IAM, encryption).

nis2-21g-04.question: Are cyber hygiene requirements documented and enforced (updates, screen lock, passwords)?
nis2-21g-04.description: Basic hygiene practices reduce the attack surface. They must be documented and enforced, not just recommended.
nis2-21g-04.guidance: Document hygiene requirements: auto-updates enabled, screen lock after 5 min, password manager required, clean desk policy.

nis2-21h-01.question: Is there a formal cryptography policy specifying approved algorithms and minimum key lengths?
nis2-21h-01.description: A cryptography policy prevents use of weak or deprecated algorithms and ensures consistent standards.
nis2-21h-01.guidance: Define approved algorithms (AES-256, RSA-2048+, SHA-256+). Ban deprecated algorithms. Review annually.

nis2-21h-02.question: Is there a key management lifecycle covering generation, rotation, revocation, and destruction?
nis2-21h-02.description: Poor key management undermines encryption. Keys must be properly managed throughout their lifecycle.
nis2-21h-02.guidance: Document key management procedures. Use HSMs for critical keys. Rotate keys per policy. Securely destroy retired keys.

nis2-21h-03.question: Is data classified with encryption requirements defined per classification level?
nis2-21h-03.description: Not all data needs the same protection. Classification drives proportionate encryption controls.
nis2-21h-03.guidance: Define data classification levels (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted). Map encryption requirements per level.

nis2-21h-04.question: Is encryption enforced at rest and in transit, with TLS 1.2+ for external communications?
nis2-21h-04.description: Data must be protected both at rest (disk/database) and in transit (network). TLS 1.2 is the minimum standard.
nis2-21h-04.guidance: Enable encryption at rest for all databases and storage. Enforce TLS 1.2+ for all external connections. Disable TLS 1.0/1.1.

nis2-21i-01.question: Is there an access control policy with least privilege, RBAC, and quarterly reviews?
nis2-21i-01.description: Access control is foundational. Least privilege limits blast radius; RBAC simplifies management; reviews catch drift.
nis2-21i-01.guidance: Document RBAC model, approval workflows, review schedule. Conduct quarterly access reviews. Remove unused access.

nis2-21i-02.question: Does onboarding include security training, NDA, and role-based provisioning before access?
nis2-21i-02.description: Consistent onboarding prevents gaps. Training and legal agreements must precede system access.
nis2-21i-02.guidance: Onboarding checklist: NDA signed, security training completed, role-based access provisioned, hardware issued.

nis2-21i-03.question: Is there same-day account revocation on departure with a formal offboarding checklist?
nis2-21i-03.description: Delayed offboarding creates risk. Departing employees must lose access immediately.
nis2-21i-03.guidance: HR notifies IT same-day. Disable accounts within 1 hour. Revoke: email, VPN, SSO, cloud services, physical badges.

nis2-21i-04.question: Is there an asset inventory (hardware, software, data) with owners and classification?
nis2-21i-04.description: You cannot protect what you do not know. A complete asset inventory is the basis for risk management.
nis2-21i-04.guidance: Maintain inventory of all hardware, software, and data assets. Assign owners. Classify by sensitivity. Review quarterly.

nis2-21i-05.question: Is privileged access managed with additional controls (PAM, time-limited sessions, enhanced logging)?
nis2-21i-05.description: Privileged accounts are prime targets for attackers. Standard access controls are insufficient for admin-level access.
nis2-21i-05.guidance: Implement PAM solution. Require just-in-time access for admin tasks. Log all privileged sessions. Review privileged access monthly.

nis2-21i-06.question: Are background or security checks performed for personnel in roles with elevated access?
nis2-21i-06.description: Personnel with privileged access or handling sensitive data pose higher risk. Pre-employment screening reduces insider threat.
nis2-21i-06.guidance: Perform background checks for privileged roles before granting access. Define which roles require checks. Review policy annually.

nis2-21j-01.question: Is MFA enforced for critical systems using hardware tokens or authenticator apps (not SMS)?
nis2-21j-01.description: SMS-based MFA is vulnerable to SIM-swap attacks. Hardware tokens or authenticator apps are required.
nis2-21j-01.guidance: Enforce MFA for all critical systems. Use hardware tokens (FIDO2/U2F) or authenticator apps. Block SMS-based MFA.

nis2-21j-02.question: Are end-to-end encrypted channels used for sensitive voice, video, and text communications?
nis2-21j-02.description: Sensitive communications must be protected from eavesdropping with end-to-end encryption.
nis2-21j-02.guidance: Use E2E encrypted tools for sensitive comms (Signal, Teams with E2E, encrypted email). Document approved channels.

nis2-21j-03.question: Are secured emergency communications operational if primary systems are compromised?
nis2-21j-03.description: If primary comms are down during an incident, you need a backup channel that is pre-established and tested.
nis2-21j-03.guidance: Establish out-of-band comms (separate messaging app, satellite phone, personal devices). Test during DR exercises.

nis2-21j-04.question: Is legacy authentication blocked and continuous/adaptive auth used for high-risk access?
nis2-21j-04.description: Legacy auth protocols bypass MFA. Adaptive auth adjusts requirements based on risk signals.
nis2-21j-04.guidance: Block legacy auth (NTLM, basic auth). Implement conditional access policies. Use adaptive MFA for high-risk logins.
